reasoning: Chief complaint of bilateral hand tingling following head trauma with facial impact suggests possible spinal cord injury (cervical spine involvement) until proven otherwise
Mechanism: diving into pool with face striking bottom creates risk for cervical spine trauma, which can present with paresthesias in extremities
Neurological symptom (tingling in both hands) in context of head/neck trauma is a high-risk presentation requiring urgent evaluation

Patient is alert and responsive, which is reassuring, but does not exclude significant spinal cord injury; incomplete injuries or central cord syndrome can present with preserved consciousness and selective neurological deficits

Vital signs are NOT RECORDED at triage — this is a critical gap. Per ESI guidelines, inability to obtain or record vitals in a potentially high-risk patient (trauma, neuro symptoms) warrants higher acuity assignment
Age 16 (adolescent) — vital sign thresholds differ from adults; however, the neurological complaint takes precedence over vital stability in this trauma context
Red flag: bilateral symmetrical paresthesias post-head trauma suggest central process (spinal cord) rather than isolated peripheral nerve injury
This patient requires immediate imaging (cervical spine imaging), physician evaluation, and possible immobilization; cannot safely wait for routine ESI-3 triage
